This split gives Multigres the context to do more than basic connection reuse. In v0.1.0, that includes per-user pools, fair-share allocation, primary routing, replica reads, multi-cell pooler discovery, failover buffering, prepared statement handling, transaction awareness, COPY support, LISTEN/NOTIFY, query cancellation, and session pinning when PostgreSQL state requires it.
v0.1.0 includes SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication, TLS for PostgreSQL client connections, mTLS for internal gRPC, password-file support,

## SQLite v1.11.0
[Diff since v1.10.0](https://github.com/JuliaDatabases/SQLite.jl/compare/v1.10.0...v1.11.0)
- `SQLite.Query`, the result of `DBInterface.execute`, is now a `DBInterface.Cursor`, so code written for `DBInterface.Cursor` applies to SQLite results too. For example, with StructUtils 2.12, `JSON.json(DBInterface.execute(db, sql))` writes the result's rows. (#376)
- Make query results subtype DBInterface.Cursor (#376) (@quinnj-bot[bot])

## SQLite v1.10.0
[Diff since v1.9.0](https://github.com/JuliaDatabases/SQLite.jl/compare/v1.9.0...v1.10.0)
- `SQLite.transaction(f, db)`, and with it `DBInterface.transaction`, `executemany` and `load!`, rolls back when the commit fails (for example with `SQLITE_BUSY`) instead of leaving the transaction open, where later statements ran inside it and were lost at close. When the failing statement already ended the transaction, its own error is reported instead of "no such savepoint" (#371).
